info.name: URL Shortener API
info.description: Create short links, verify redirects and click analytics, and check validation and alias-conflict behavior. Start shortener-service on localhost:8081 first.

request.description: Creates a short link. If the alias already exists, change the collection variable `alias` and resend.

exec: pm.test('response includes short URL and target', function () { pm.expect(body.shortUrl).to.include(body.code); pm.expect(body.targetUrl).to.eql('https://example.com/a-long-page'); });

request.description: Records a click and returns a 302 Location header. Redirect following is disabled for this request so Postman can assert the 302.

exec: pm.test('short URL redirects to the target', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(302); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Location')).to.eql('https://example.com/a-long-page'); });

request.description: Run after following the short URL. Analytics include total clicks, referrer host counts, and daily counts.

exec: pm.test('analytics reports the redirect click', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.code).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('code')); pm.expect(body.totalClicks).to.be.at.least(1); pm.expect(body.dailyClicks).to.be.an('array'); });

request.description: Run after request 1. The alias was already created, so the API should return HTTP 409.

exec: pm.test('duplicate alias is rejected', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(409); });

request.description: Confirms that only absolute HTTP and HTTPS target URLs are accepted.

exec: pm.test('unsafe URL scheme is rejected', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(400); });
